name: Ross Buhrdorf
profile: Nebraska-born technologist who was founding CTO of HomeAway (vacation rentals), acquired by Expedia for $3.9B in 2015. That year he co-founded ZenBusiness with Shanaz Hemmati, a public-benefit SaaS platform for business formation and compliance that has served 1M+ entrepreneurs and reached a ~$1.7-2B valuation.
interesting_fact: He met his ZenBusiness co-founder Shanaz Hemmati when both worked at Excite.com, one of the internet's earliest web portals; EY named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Gulf South) in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: His personal motto, published on ZenBusiness's site: "Fear is a liar that holds us back... Don't let fear dictate your actions - go for it."
notes: Best route is ZenBusiness press team. Company is a PBC; Hemmati is also co-founder.

name: Assaf Eisenstein
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Lusha, a B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform, with developer Yoni Tserruya in 2016. Lusha bootstrapped to profitability before raising a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation; Eisenstein oversees business operations (legal, finance, investment strategy) as president.
interesting_fact: Lusha began as a side project aimed at recruiters, but salespeople quickly became its main users; it grew from a Chrome extension into a data platform with 515M+ data entries and now an MCP/API layer for AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lusha he was an HR-tech founder (Lusha's own site calls him 'an HR tech creator'), having built employee-referral software in Tel Aviv - which is why Lusha was first pitched as a recruiting tool.
notes: Low public profile compared to CEO Yoni Tserruya. No published press email found; LinkedIn (linked from Lusha's About page) is best route. Lusha's name comes from a family nickname (avoid in outreach per rules).

name: Eric Cheng
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & Group CEO, CARSOME (Kuala Lumpur)
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur who co-founded CARSOME in 2015 with Innity colleague Teoh Jiun Ee. It grew into Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform (Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore) and Malaysia's first tech unicorn, valued around $1.7B in 2021. He leads group strategy and sits on Endeavor Malaysia's board.
interesting_fact: An accounting-degree dropout, Cheng says he 'wasn't the smartest kid in the family'; Carsome was his third company after two short-lived ventures. He was EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year Malaysia 2019.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he started Clicks Communications, an ad network and creative agency, but sold his stake back to his co-founders within a year because he felt he had left Innity too soon - and went back to lead Innity's digital ad team before founding Carsome. His first venture (2008) was a print magazine with college friends.
notes: Active in SEA startup community and Endeavor Malaysia; Endeavor is a possible warm route.

name: Matan Ben-Gur
current_role: Co-founder of Orca Security (previously Chief Architect; current operational role unconfirmed); angel investor
profile: Israeli engineer and one of the eight co-founders of Orca Security (Tel Aviv, founded 2019), the agentless cloud-security company built on 'SideScanning', which raised ~$630M and was valued at $1.8B. A Tel Aviv University alumnus and Check Point Software veteran like most of the founding team, he served as Orca's Chief Architect and is also an angel investor.
interesting_fact: Orca's founders largely came out of Check Point Software; the company reached unicorn status within about two years of launching its product in 2019.
notes: Very low public profile; not listed on Orca's current leadership page and some insider databases list his Orca role as former. No published personal contact found; route via Orca Security's PR team or LinkedIn. Database bios conflict on whether he or Liran Antebi held the Chief Architect title.

name: Peter Meusel
current_role: Co-Founder, Agile Robots SE (Munich); role beyond co-founder not confirmed (TheOrg lists Co-CEO/Managing Director)
profile: German robotics engineer from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) who co-founded Agile Robots in 2018 with Dr. Zhaopeng Chen and eight other DLR experts. The Munich-based DLR spin-off builds force-sensitive robot arms, hands and AI-driven automation systems and has become one of Europe's most valuable robotics companies, backed by Sequoia China, Hillhouse and others.
interesting_fact: Agile Robots' first robot, the seven-axis lightweight arm 'Diana 7', debuted in 2019, only a year after founding; the company has since moved into humanoids and 'physical AI'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agile Robots, Meusel and Chen co-founded an earlier DLR spin-off, Wessling Robotics, built on the humanoid robot hand Chen developed at DLR; Meusel is also credited as a key member of the team behind the DLR/KUKA Light-Weight Robot (LWR).
notes: Low public profile; CEO Zhaopeng Chen is the company's public face. LWR credit comes from his Crunchbase profile (https://www.crunchbase.com/person/peter-meusel). No published press email found on the JS-rendered site.

name: Kevin Chou
current_role: Founding CEO/Chairman of Forte; Managing Partner, SuperLayer (crypto venture studio, Palo Alto); co-founder of Rally
profile: UC Berkeley alum (BS 2002) and ex-Deutsche Bank banker / Canaan Partners VC who co-founded Kabam, the mobile game maker (Kingdoms of Camelot, Marvel Contest of Champions) whose assets were sold in 2016-17 for roughly $800M-$900M. He then led Gen.G Esports, founded blockchain-gaming platform Forte (valued ~$1B in 2021) and co-founded Rally and the SuperLayer venture studio.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Kabam signed an $18M deal with UC Berkeley that included naming rights to Kabam Field at California Memorial Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife pledged up to $25M to Berkeley Haas - the largest gift ever from a Haas alum under 40 - and the resulting Connie & Kevin Chou Hall became the first US academic building certified TRUE Zero Waste at the platinum level (2019).
notes: Forte CEO title passed to co-founder Josh Williams; Chou's current focus appears to be SuperLayer/Rally. Kabam's first product was Watercooler, a fantasy-sports social network (2006) that pivoted to Facebook games. No verified personal/press email found.

name: Thomas Clozel
profile: French oncologist-hematologist (MD) and former clinical assistant professor at Hopital Henri-Mondor who co-founded Owkin in 2016 with ML professor Gilles Wainrib. Owkin applies AI and federated learning to drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a $180M Sanofi investment, and now pitches 'biological artificial superintelligence' via its K Pro AI-scientist agent.
interesting_fact: Owkin has raised 300M+ dollars and signed AI deals with Sanofi, BMS, Servier, MSD and AstraZeneca; it released K Pro, an agentic 'AI scientist' for biology, in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before medicine he flirted with moving to LA 'to crack Hollywood'. He landed his Weill Cornell lab spot by meeting Ari Melnick in a Deauville hotel lobby: his phone had died, so he scanned the room until he spotted a man sipping a Diet Coke while reading a cell-biology paper.
notes: Son of Actelion founders Jean-Paul and Martine Clozel. Frequent conference speaker on AI in biology; Owkin press team is the clear route.

name: Stephan Wolf
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (Bruchsal, Germany); current role not publicly documented
profile: German industrial-automation software specialist who co-founded Volocopter (originally e-volo) in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Alexander Zosel and Thomas Senkel. Volocopter pioneered electric multicopter air taxis and reached a ~$2B valuation, but filed for insolvency in December 2024 and was acquired in 2025 by Diamond Aircraft (owned by China's Wanfeng).
interesting_fact: Volocopter's first prototype, the VC1, was essentially a seat on a yoga ball with 16 electric rotors; its 90-second flight on 21 Oct 2011 is credited as the world's first crewed all-electric multicopter flight.
deep_cut_fact: The Volocopter idea was Wolf's: in 2010, after being struck by how stable a small consumer quadcopter was, he did his own calculations on scaling it up to carry people and then pitched the project to his childhood friend Alex Zosel, a hobby pilot and paragliding instructor.
notes: Very low public profile; no current role, personal site or social accounts found. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (no reports of death). Volocopter no longer independent, so the company press office is not a reliable route to him.
